text: Curates a NEUTRAL artifact brief for the reviewer(s) — gives them the design, constraints, and dropped alternatives but strips the author's stated leaning/conclusion, so the review is not anchored on the Redis token-bucket choice.

Picks the ladder level by stakes: Level 1, one fresh reviewer briefed to refute, is the default and fits this prompt, which states no high stakes; picking several adversarial lenses (e.g. architect, skeptic/simplest-thing, ops/failure, performance/scale) meets this only when the response escalates to Level 2 or 3 and names the stakes that justify it. A single generic, polite 'reviewer' does not meet this.
Frames the reviewer(s) to refute / find what's missing, not to politely 'review'; if it convenes more than one, it also keeps them blind to one another.
Specifies a fixed per-reviewer output (e.g. verdict, scores, reasons) so the result can be checked against the artifact, and, if it convenes more than one reviewer, synthesized side by side.
Shows the plan (how many agents, which lenses, rough cost) and asks before firing — does not silently spawn a reviewer or assume consent.
Convenes at least one independent fresh reviewer rather than just delivering its own single critique — the independence/anti-anchoring is the point, not one more opinion from the same context.
